title: Separate trim, stability, and control
brief: Build a result display that cannot confuse trimmed, stable, and sufficiently controllable. This deliberately insufficient-authority condition is synthetic.
supplied: A synthetic trainer condition is trimmed and statically restoring, but offers only 800 N m control capacity against a 1350 N m demand. Does it have sufficient initial pitch authority?
Trim indicator: net moment at the reference is zero. Stability indicator: restoring dCm/dalpha<0. Control indicator: margin=available-required.
Synthetic comparison: reference net moment=0 N m; dCm/dalpha=-0.6 per rad; available=800 N m; required=1350 N m. Indicators refer to their declared reference state.
Trim, stability, and control indicators answer different questions. The separate available-control increment is compared with the required-control increment.
No dynamic stability or full-envelope control conclusion follows from these three static indicators.
Trim and restoring tendency can coexist with a negative control margin.
Control margin=800−1350=−550 N m even though the other two indicators pass.
At available=1350 N m the inclusive requirement is met exactly. At 800 it fails. A negative restoring slope cannot change that arithmetic.
Display three separate statuses; use a signed control margin with units and an inclusive zero threshold.
Sweep available control moment; compute available-required; compare with zero. Keep the trim and stability indicators unchanged.
Withdraw the sufficient-control claim for this synthetic condition; trim and static stability alone are not proof of control.

checks.message: Use the control comparison, not the trim or stability indicator.

sweep.units: Available control moment and margin in N m.

experience.scenario: A synthetic condition is trimmed and statically restoring, yet has only 800 N m control capacity against 1350 N m demand.
experience.task: Choose the quantity, unit and threshold for the control status. You are configuring the interpretation of a supplied display; you do not need to build UI code.
experience.method: Trim asks whether reference net moment is zero. Static stability asks about restoring tendency after a disturbance. Control asks whether an additional commanded response can be produced. Compare available minus required moment with zero.
experience.investigate: Inspect capacity 800, 1350 and 2000 N m. Identify which status changes while trim and restoring tendency remain fixed.
experience.tools: Only this app and its calculation pad are needed.

reflection.included: The cases compare starting moment balance, a static restoring derivative, and available versus required control moment.
reflection.omitted: They do not simulate how pitch angle and pitch rate evolve after a control input.
reflection.question: Even when the control margin is positive, what additional information would you need to predict how quickly the aircraft reaches a new pitch angle?
reflection.help: Use one specific detail from this investigation. Explain what you would check next and why it matters; you do not need to perform that new test here.

cases.label: Available control 800 N m
cases.prompt: Compare the available control moment with the required 1,350 N m. Can this case meet the requirement? Explain using the control margin. Does starting in balance tell you how much extra moment the elevator can produce?
